  **Bottom line:** Margin Notes won't boot on pagy 9.3.5 as it stands. The upgrade needs three small code changes, made in one commit with the gem bump: the initializer, one view line and one controller line. With those changes the full suite passes (46 runs, 0 failures). I also requested the `/notes` page on both versions with the same inputs, and it behaved the same apart from the wording of one error message. Only the controller line can land first, on 8.6.3. Pagy touches no stored data or queued work, so rollout and rollback are simple. The working repository was not modified (`git status` is clean).
  
  Pagy appears in only six places:
  - `Gemfile` and `Gemfile.lock`
  - `config/initializers/pagy.rb`
  - `app/controllers/notes_controller.rb`, which includes `Pagy::Backend` and calls `pagy(@notes)`
  - `app/helpers/application_helper.rb`, which includes `Pagy::Frontend`
  - `app/views/notes/index.html.erb`, which uses `@pagy.items`, `@pagy.count`, `@pagy.pages`, `prev`/`next`, `pagy_info(item_name:)` and `pagy_url_for(pagy, page)`
  
  Nothing uses pagy's built-in page-link helpers (`pagy_nav` and similar), its JavaScript helpers, the `size` option, the i18n extra, or pagy keys in `config/locales/en.yml`. So the 9.0 changes to the nav, series, `size` format and JavaScript helpers don't apply to this app.
  
  ## Required changes (all with the gem bump)
  
  **R1. The `items` extra no longer exists, so the app fails at boot.**
  - **Where:** `config/initializers/pagy.rb`.
  - **Evidence:** 9.3.5 has no `lib/pagy/extras/items.rb`. It was replaced by `limit.rb`, which uses `DEFAULT[:limit_param]` and `DEFAULT[:limit_max]`. Running the unchanged app on 9.3.5 failed with `cannot load such file -- pagy/extras/items (LoadError)`.
  - **Change:**
    - `require "pagy/extras/items"` becomes `require "pagy/extras/limit"`
    - `Pagy::DEFAULT[:items]` becomes `Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit]` (keep 10)
    - `:items_param` becomes `:limit_param` (keep `:per_page`)
    - `:max_items` becomes `:limit_max` (keep 50)
    - Keep `overflow` and `:last_page` as they are.
  - **Works on 8.6.3?** No. 8.6.3 has no `limit` extra, so this must ship with the bump.
  - **Watch out:** pagy silently ignores an unknown `DEFAULT` key. Keeping `:max_items` would quietly drop the 50 cap and fall back to 9's default of 100, with no error. The existing test that requests `per_page=500` catches this, so keep it.
  
  **R2. `Pagy#items` is gone.**
  - **Where:** `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30`.
  - **Change:** `@pagy.items` becomes `@pagy.limit`. In 9.3.5, `shared_methods.rb` provides `attr_reader :page, :limit, :vars`.
  - **Works on 8.6.3?** No. Ship with the bump.
  
  **R3. Invalid page numbers now raise an error instead of showing page 1.**
  - **Where:** `NotesController#index`.
  - **Evidence:** In 8.6.3, `pagy_get_page` returns `[params[...].to_i, 1].max`. In 9.3.5 it returns `(page || 1).to_i`, and `Pagy#initialize` raises when the page is below 1. With only R1 and R2 applied, the test "invalid pages show the first page..." fails with `Pagy::VariableError: expected :page >= 1; got 0`. A blank `page` still works because 9 drops blank values, but `0`, `-1` and `two` raise. `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the fall-back-to-page-1 behavior.
  - **Change:** `@pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes, page: [params[:page].to_i, 1].max)`. Overriding the private `pagy_get_page` in the controller would also work, but passing the page explicitly is simpler.
  - **Works on 8.6.3?** Yes. The full suite passed on 8.6.3 with this line (46 runs, 0 failures), so it can land first as a preparatory commit.
  
  **R4. Update the documentation.**
  - `ARCHITECTURE.md:17-23` and `docs/guides/controllers.md:108` say "Pagy 8.6.3".
  - `ARCHITECTURE.md:23` mentions `Pagy::VariableError`, which is still accurate. Only the message text changes, from `:items` to `:limit`.
  
  ## Behavior checked beyond the suite (executed)
  
  I wrote a throwaway test that requested `/notes` with 32 notes on both versions. Inputs:
  - no parameters, and `page=2`
  - `per_page` set to blank, `0`, `-3`, `abc`, `7` and `500`
  - `page` set to `99`, `2.9` and `1e2`
  
  Both versions returned the same status, note count, range text and selected page size. The next and previous URLs matched exactly, including parameter order: `/notes?page=2&per_page=10` normally, and `/notes?per_page=7&page=2` when `per_page` was in the request. Overflow to the last page and the 50 cap also matched.
  
  The one difference is the text of the error raised for an invalid `per_page`: `expected :items >= 1` on 8.6.3 versus `expected :limit >= 1` on 9.3.5.   - **New 9.x features** (the keyset paginator, `limit_extra` toggles, `pagy_limit_selector_js`): none are needed. Keep the current defaults, as CLAUDE.md requires.
